description: Static-typing contrast for the PiCC construction task: TypeScript under `tsc --strict` versus plain JavaScript on the same Node.js 24 runtime, with prompts, specification, tests, reference access, and budgets held at the starter baseline. Second manifest version (v7 cohort): revised oracle (preprocessed inputs, corpus macro and stage-averaged fuzz macro as co-primary endpoints) and the bash default timeout (image 0.4, Pi 0.85.1, @cad0p/pi-bash-timeout@0.1.0); the v4 cohort (picc-types-v1) ran on image 0.2 without either.

provenance.creator: study-author
provenance.source: PiCC task contract and Writing a C Compiler test-suite scope

conditions.description: Plain JavaScript on Node.js 24 with no type annotations and no static type checker; the build step is a syntax check only. Behavioral specification in TASK.md, detailed workflow prompt, failure-level test tool, empty repository, and no reference implementation, as in the starter baseline.

TypeScript on the same Node.js 24 runtime with explicit type annotations required and `tsc --strict --noEmitOnError` as the build gate: a snapshot that does not type-check has no compiler. Differs from js-untyped only in the candidate adapter.
